Thank you for contributing to TiDB! Please read TiDB's [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) document **BEFORE** filing this PR.
-->

### What problem does this PR solve? <!--add issue link with summary if exists-->

Fix https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/10081

### What is changed and how it works?

- Add a new struct for representing the analyze job info.
- Record all the analyze jobs in the stats handle.
- Update the job info when we receive one response from tikv.

The final result is like:
```sql
MySQL [test]> show analyze status;
+--------------+------------+----------------+-------------------+-----------+---------------------+---------+
| Table_schema | Table_name | Partition_name | Job_info          | Row_count | Start_time          | State   |
+--------------+------------+----------------+-------------------+-----------+---------------------+---------+
| test         | t          |                | analyze index idx |         0 | 2019-04-17 16:37:10 | succeed |
| test         | t          |                | analyze columns   |         0 | 2019-04-17 16:37:10 | succeed |
+--------------+------------+----------------+-------------------+-----------+---------------------+---------+
2 rows in set (0.001 sec)

MySQL [test]> select * from information_schema.analyze_status;
+--------------+------------+----------------+-------------------+-----------+---------------------+---------+
| TABLE_SCHEMA | TABLE_NAME | PARTITION_NAME | JOB_INFO          | ROW_COUNT | START_TIME          | STATE   |
+--------------+------------+----------------+-------------------+-----------+---------------------+---------+
| test         | t          |                | analyze columns   |         0 | 2019-04-17 16:37:10 | succeed |
| test         | t          |                | analyze index idx |         0 | 2019-04-17 16:37:10 | succeed |
+--------------+------------+----------------+-------------------+-----------+---------------------+---------+
2 rows in set (0.001 sec)

```

issue_context.title: Support to show analyze status
issue_context.body:
## Feature Request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...] -->
To help DBAs know the progress of the `ANALYZE` statement.

**Describe the feature you'd like:**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
Implement some SQL like `admin show analyze`.
It can return that how many regions information have been collected.
comments: Why not just estimated progress in `show processlist` output?

@winoros Others have used the `State` column for this:
https://www.percona.com/blog/2009/11/17/new-tokudb-2-2-0-feature-more-query-progress-information/

Currently `2` means `autocommit`, which is not very useful. I would love to see us do something more with this column :-)

**Edit:** A single value `state` will frequently not map correctly to TiDB, since many things happen in parallel. It makes a lot of sense for MySQL since everything is single threaded.

review_comments: `database_name` is more common on the user side.
It keeps the convention with others in this file.
No, because they processed the same rows, and we just split the row into different collectors.

It's better to sort the result of analyze status on `Start_time` in descending order to let the latest records appear on the bottom of the result. Take this as an example: As you can see in the picture, there are a lot of history informations which exceeds a full screen. If users want to take a look at the latest analyze jobs, they have to scroll the screen up. Which I think is somehow inconvenient. In order to see the running jobs, we have to use `show analyze status where state = "running";` at present. If we sort the result in the descending order of `start_time`, the last records are running analyze jobs if there are. Thus the command can be simplified to `show analyze status`

Some tables have fewer rows, thus newer start time does not mean they are running. Instead, the result is already sorted by their status update time, see  https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/10172/files#diff-318b1ef9098a111a1e7f8b3784db7fb2R89
OK. We should use update time indeed. How about sort the result in the descending order of `update_time`?
I think it already sorts the result in the descending order of update_time at https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/10172/files#diff-318b1ef9098a111a1e7f8b3784db7fb2R89.
:joy: I wish the latest record appears in the last, it should be ascending order.

Can we execute `MoveToHistory` here?

Because when I execute ` analyze table t1,t2,t_slim,t_wide;`, 

Then I may got result like below:

```sql

tidb > select * from `ANALYZE_STATUS`;
+--------------+------------+----------------+-----------------+----------------+---------------------+----------+
| TABLE_SCHEMA | TABLE_NAME | PARTITION_NAME | JOB_INFO        | PROCESSED_ROWS | START_TIME          | STATE    |
+--------------+------------+----------------+-----------------+----------------+---------------------+----------+
| test         | t_slim     |                | analyze columns | 10000          | 2019-04-24 10:49:22 | finished |
| test         | t1         |                | analyze columns | 0              | 2019-04-24 10:49:22 | finished |
| test         | t2         |                | analyze columns | 0              | 2019-04-24 10:49:22 | finished |
| test         | t_wide     |                | analyze columns | 0              | 2019-04-24 10:49:22 | running  |
```
No, the history size is limited, so some tasks that belong to the same analyze statement may be removed before the whole is done.
